transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I, uh... I hope I'm in the right place for this. It’s a little embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I don't want to make a big fuss, but... well, I've been having these times where I just eat way too much. 

What really brings me in today is that after I do it, I just sit there looking at all the empty containers and wrappers, and I feel so... disgusted with myself. I've always prided myself on being a steady, in-control kind of man, you know? Out on the road driving my routes, taking care of business... and when I'm looking at that mess, I just feel like I'm not that man at all. 

Does that make sense? I just really hope it's something you can help me figure out.
After these episodes of eating too much, do you ever try to make up for it by doing something to counteract the effects of the food?

Make up for it? Um... no, not really. I mean, if you mean... like making myself sick, or taking something to get it out of my system? No, I've never done anything like that. I don't do anything extreme. 

I mostly just... well, like I said, I just sit there feeling pretty awful about myself. Since I'm driving the truck most of the day, I can't exactly go to a gym and run it off, either. I just kind of live with the guilt, I guess, and try to promise myself I'll be better the next day. 

Is... is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these episodes where you eat too much?

Well, I... I try to be in control. I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just completely reckless or anything. I'm usually a very disciplined guy. But... to be completely honest with you, once I start eating during those times, it's like... it feels like that same discipline I have out on the road just sort of shuts off. 

I'll actually be sitting there in the cab or at home, literally telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down. You've had enough.' But... my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. It's really hard to admit that to you, a grown man not being able to stop his own hand. I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's happening.
How often do these episodes of eating too much happen?

Well, uh... I guess it happens more than I'd like to admit. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, but... since I've been stuck at home with this back injury, it's gotten a bit more frequent. 

I'd say it happens, you know, several nights most weeks. I try really hard to have good weeks, but... if I'm being completely honest, I can't really think of a single week in the last three months where I didn't have at least one of these... episodes. 

I know that probably sounds like a lot, and I'm really trying to get a handle on it. I hope that's the kind of detail you need? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate timeline so you can help me.
Do these episodes of eating too much usually happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset about something?

Well, I... I guess I wouldn't really say it's just when I'm upset. I mean, I try to handle stress pretty well, you know? Being a driver, you kind of have to roll with the punches. 

So, it's not like I'm having a breakdown every time I eat too much. It just sort of... happens. Sometimes I'm just sitting there watching TV, not really feeling anxious at all, and I still end up eating more than I should. I don't want you to think I'm an overly emotional guy who can't handle his problems. 

Is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way. I know some people eat their feelings, but I don't think that's exactly what's going on with me.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?

Well, I... I think we kind of touched on that a little bit earlier, didn't we? I mean, I really don't want to sound like a broken record, or like I'm just completely out of control. 

But, um... yeah, like I was saying before, once I get going, it's... it's incredibly hard to just put the brakes on. I try, I really do try to stop myself. But it's like my hand has a mind of its own. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out.
Do you usually feel guilty or self-critical after these episodes of eating too much?

Well, um... I guess this is the hardest part to admit. I really don't want you to think less of me, you know? I've always prided myself on being a steady, dependable guy... the kind of man who has things under control. 

But... yeah. Honestly, that's a big part of why I'm here. After it happens, I just... I sit there looking at all the empty wrappers and containers, and I just feel so... disgusted with myself. It's a terrible feeling, like I've completely let myself down. I don't want to sound dramatic, but it really eats at me. 

I hope it's okay that I'm being this honest with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, even the parts I'm not proud of.
Do you think your mood or emotional state plays a role in when these episodes of eating too much happen?

Well, um... I know we talked a little bit about stress earlier, and I... I really don't want to frustrate you by saying the same thing again. But honestly, I don't really think my mood has much to do with it. 

I've always been a pretty even-keeled guy, you know? I don't really get too high or too low. So, it's not like I'm feeling sad or angry or anything when I start eating. Sometimes I'm in a perfectly good mood, just resting up after a long shift on the road, and it still happens. I just haven't really noticed a pattern with my emotions. 

I'm... I'm not sure if that's the answer you're looking for? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a very clear reason for why this is happening. I can definitely try to pay more attention to my moods if you think that's something I should be doing? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Well, I... I know we've kind of circled around this, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just completely falling apart or anything. I mean, out on the road, I'm disciplined. I have to be. I manage my routes, my time, everything. 

But when I'm eating like that... it's like all that discipline just shuts off. I'll actually be sitting there, telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down. You don't need this.' But... my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. It's embarrassing to admit that to you, honestly. A man my age should have better control. 

I hope I'm making sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you can understand what's happening.
Do you feel like you're eating in response to an emotional need during these episodes?

Well, um... I know you just asked about my mood a minute ago, and I don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm not listening to you. I really am trying to give you the best answers I can. 

But... no, I really don't think it's an emotional thing. Like I said, I'm a pretty steady guy. I don't get all worked up about things. I know sometimes people eat when they're upset or lonely, but... that just doesn't feel like what's happening with me. It's more like... I just start eating, and then I can't stop, regardless of how I'm feeling inside. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a better explanation for you? I know doctors usually like to find a root cause for these things, and I feel bad that I can't point to an emotion and say, 'That's it.' Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Do you feel like you're losing control over your eating during these episodes?

Well, um... I know we touched on this just a second ago, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or wasting your time. I know you have a lot of patients to see. 

But yes, I guess... I guess "losing control" is probably the right way to put it. It's just so strange for me, because out on the road, I'm the guy who has everything under control, you know? I have to be. But once I start eating during these... times... it's like all that discipline just completely shuts off. 

I'll literally be sitting there, fully aware, telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down. You don't need this.' But... my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. It's like I'm watching myself do it and I can't stop it. It's really hard to admit that out loud, because I know I should be stronger than that. 

I hope that answers your question better? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can figure this out. I'm trying my best to be clear for you.
Have these episodes of eating too much been happening for more than 3 months?

Well, let's see... I hope I'm getting the timeline right for you, I don't want to give you bad information. But, um, yeah, I'd say it's been right around that three-month mark. 

It all really started when I strained my back and they had to take me off the road. Being stuck at home instead of driving my routes... I guess that's when this whole eating thing kind of snuck up on me. It's been about three months since the injury, so that lines up. 

I really hope that's the kind of detail you're looking for? I know doctors need accurate timelines, and I'm trying to be as precise as I can so I'm not making your job harder. Does that three-month timeframe make sense with what you usually see?
Do you consider these episodes of eating too much to be times when you're eating an amount of food that's definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time frame?

Well, um... I really want to be honest with you here, even though it's a little embarrassing to admit. I hope you don't judge me too harshly for this, I really am trying to be a good patient for you. 

But... yeah, I suppose it is a lot more than a normal person would eat. Like, some evenings, I'll tell myself I'm just going to heat up what I swear is just one bowl of pozole, you know? Just a regular portion. But then... before I even really realize what's happening, I've gone through the entire pot. And then maybe a couple of tamales, and chips, and... well, whatever leftovers are sitting there in the kitchen. It's honestly like I'm feeding a whole crew instead of just myself. 

I know that's probably not what you want to hear, and I feel awful even saying it out loud to you. I should be managing things better. Am I giving you the right kind of details, though? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need to know so I'm not making your job any harder.
Do these episodes of eating too much cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life or relationships?

Well, um... I really hope I'm not sounding like I'm complaining too much. I know I should just be handling this better, and I don't want to seem like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. But... yes, it does bother me quite a bit. 

It's just... well, I was supposed to be mentoring some of the newer drivers, you know? Since I'm off the road right now. But lately, I've... I've started letting their check-in calls go to voicemail. I just feel so ashamed of myself, and I don't want them hearing it in my voice, or finding out how far off my routine I've gotten. I'm supposed to be the guy setting an example, and instead I'm just hiding out at home. 

I feel terrible about letting them down, and I know I should be doing better. I hope it's okay that I shared that with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it doesn't make me look very good. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you experienced these episodes of eating too much at least once a week for the past three months?

Well... gosh, I really wish I could tell you no, I really do. I know I should be doing better than this, and I hope you aren't too disappointed in me. But, um... yeah, it's definitely been at least once a week. 

Honestly, since I've been stuck at home with this back injury, it's been happening several nights most weeks. I've been trying to keep track, just so I could give you good information, and... well, I really can't think of a single week in these whole three months where I didn't have at least one of those episodes. 

I'm really trying to get a handle on it, I promise. I know it's not good. I just hope I'm giving you the right kind of timeline? I want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for your notes. Does that answer what you needed to know?
Do you feel like you're unable to control your eating during these episodes because you can't resist the food or because you feel like something is driving you to continue eating?

Well, um... I hope this doesn't make me sound completely hopeless. I really am trying to be disciplined, just like I always was when I was driving. I want you to know I'm not usually like this. 

But... yeah, it's like... once I start, it feels like that discipline just completely shuts off. It's the strangest thing. Even while I'm sitting there, literally telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down, you've had enough,' my hand just... it just keeps going back for more. It's like I can't stop it, even though my brain knows I should. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I feel so weak even admitting it to you. I should have better self-control at my age. I'm really trying, I promise. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Do you feel guilty or self-critical during these episodes of eating too much because you feel like you've lost control over your eating?

Well... gosh, I really hate to admit this part. I hope you won't think too badly of me, because I've always prided myself on being a steady, dependable kind of guy, you know? The one people can count on to keep it together. 

But... yes. That's actually the main reason I finally decided I needed to come in and see you. When it's over, and I'm just... sitting there, looking at all the empty containers... I just feel so incredibly disgusted with myself. The guilt is just awful. It's like I'm looking at someone else's mess, and I can't believe I'm the one who did it. I feel like I've completely lost that steady, in-control man I've always tried so hard to be. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I really am trying to keep a positive attitude about getting better. I hope it's okay that I'm being so honest about how bad it makes me feel? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the pieces you need to help me fix this.
Do you think your eating too much is ever in response to feeling emotional?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses. I've always tried to be the kind of guy who just deals with things, you know? Not someone who lets his feelings push him around. 

But... honestly? I'm not really sure if it's tied to my emotions. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. It's more just... being stuck at home with this back thing, not out on the road where I belong. It's just... frustrating, I guess? But I wouldn't say I'm eating because I'm sad or angry or anything like that. At least, I don't think I am. 

I really hope that's an okay answer? I just haven't really put two and two together in that way, but if you think I should be paying closer attention to my feelings before it happens, I can definitely start doing that. I want to make sure I'm doing everything right to help you figure this out.
Do you think your episodes of eating too much are ever triggered by a specific emotional state, such as feeling bored, anxious, or depressed?

Well, gosh, I... I don't really know if I can pinpoint it to one of those specific feelings. I hope that's alright to say. I know you're looking for a reason, and I really wish I could give you a better answer. 

Like I said before, I'm just mostly sitting around the house these days because of my back. So, I mean, maybe I'm a little bored? But I wouldn't say I'm sitting there feeling depressed or super anxious and then deciding to eat. It's just... I'm just not doing much of anything, and the food is there. 

I'm really trying to be mindful of it, though. I don't want you to think I'm just ignoring my feelings or anything like that. I've always tried to keep a pretty even keel. Does that make sense? I can try to keep a closer eye on if I'm feeling down or worried right before it happens, if that's what you think would be best.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your eating during these episodes because you can't resist the food?

Well, gosh... I, um... I really want to be completely honest with you, even though it's a little embarrassing to say out loud. I hope you don't think I'm just weak-willed or anything, because I've always prided myself on having good self-control. You have to have a lot of it when you're driving long hours out on the road. 

But... yeah. With this... it's like, once I start, it feels like that same discipline I had on the road just completely shuts off. I'll actually be sitting there, literally telling myself in my head, 'Magin, put the fork down,' but... my hand just keeps going back for more. It's like I just can't resist it once I get going, no matter how hard I try to reason with myself. 

Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining it right for you. I just want you to know I really am trying my best to fight it, even when it gets away from me like that.
